description: Expected outcomes for the gatebraid/gate-run@2 fixture set. Every expectation below was MEASURED against the frozen schemas with CPython 3.12.2 / jsonschema 4.23.0 and recorded from that run, not asserted from reading. An invalid case names the EXACT AND COMPLETE set of (keyword, path, schema_path, property, extra_count) loci: the runner requires every recorded locus to fire and rejects any locus that fires but was not recorded. A fixture rejected for the wrong reason is not a kill, and an over-mutated fixture that fails for four reasons while the corpus records one is a defect the corpus must surface rather than absorb. Amended at M3 batch N1C (A3): a locus is now (keyword, path, schema_path, property, extra_count) and every `required` expectation records WHICH property is missing, derived from the validator's own per-property error rather than written by hand. This manifest was rewritten by that amendment even though its own cases were not the ones the ruling named: the runner raises a structure error on any `required` expectation lacking `property`, so leaving it untouched would have made the whole corpus exit 2. A forced consequence, recorded rather than presented as a discretionary extension. Amended at M3 batch N1D: a locus additionally carries the error's `schema_path` (D6 — an instance path cannot say which branch of a conditional fired) and, for `additionalProperties`, an `extra_count` (external review R1 — one and two unexpected properties produced identical loci, so an over-mutated fixture passed a manifest recording one). Every locus in this file was re-measured against the N1D-amended schemas, not carried forward.

known_limitation: ONE residual collision, MEASURED at M3 batch N1D by sweeping every corpus for identical (schema, locus set) pairs. **GR2-09 and GR2-12 share `required@(root):stop_record [allOf/2/then/required]`.** This is not a granularity defect and D6's schema path does not touch it: both are the SAME branch of one conditional — `result` in {stopped, blocked} requires `stop_record` — reached by two different enum values. No locus refinement separates two values failing one constraint, and echoing the values into a locus is barred by spec §4. It is EC1-28/EC1-29's shape exactly. **Worth stating plainly: ingesting the external review's GR2-12 CREATED this pair.** The case is still worth having — GR2-09 covered only the `stopped` arm and the `blocked` arm was untested — but a validator rejecting one for the other's reason passes both, and that is disclosed rather than absorbed. Comparison note: two cases in DIFFERENT corpora can print the same locus string (GR2-14/EC1-34 and GR2-15/EC1-35 both read `pattern@started_at`/`pattern@ended_at`) and are NOT collisions — they validate against different schemas, and the runner never compares a case against another corpus's case. A first sweep here reported them as collisions because it keyed on the locus alone; keyed on (schema, locus) the count is one. F4 DISCLOSURE (N1D): the two EXCLUSIONS (a decidable stop may not carry `workflow`; an error stop may not carry `next_approval`) are over-grounded — gate-0/1/3 contracts state them and gate-3 adds 'No Next Approval is set: the error branch does not use one'. The two REQUIREMENTS go further than the reviewer's smallest direction, which was the exclusions plus a separate adjudication of mandatoriness. The cost is named rather than left implicit: gate-0-contract action 1 makes an unreadable remote an ERROR disposition, and a gate that cannot reach the control plane cannot write `Workflow = Blocked` — yet its stop_record now must assert it. That is the ADR-0019 class this same schema invokes when it refuses a const on approvals[].author. Recorded for operator ruling: keep both requirements, or keep only the exclusions.
